title: Establish prioritized intake funnel for enterprise SDK requests (languages, auth, streaming ergonomics)
creator: Grace Huang
description:
Background: Over Q4–Q1 we saw a surge of enterprise requests for SDK language bindings, streaming ergonomics (resume, backpressure, resumable sessions), and a set of recurring auth patterns (SSO token rotation, short-lived credentials, proxy gateways). These requests arrive via sales notes, support tickets, and direct customer engineering asks. Current intake is ad hoc and engineers are triaging directly in GitHub threads which creates duplicate work and unclear prioritization for Dedicated/Private customers.

Objective: Design and implement a repeatable intake funnel and prioritization rubric for enterprise SDK/client library requests that balances: (1) customer revenue/strategic importance, (2) engineering cost/risk, (3) cross-platform reach (language coverage), and (4) compatibility with Redwood Dedicated and Private deployment constraints. The funnel should produce a ranked backlog, clear acceptance criteria, and a roadmap entry/commit decision for each high-priority request.

Scope: This ticket covers intake process definition, scoring rubric, minimal data collection form, a triage workflow (PM -> Eng -> Design decision gates), and a small pilot with 8 active enterprise requests. Implementation of SDK changes is out of scope; this ticket results in prioritization decisions and handoff artifacts.

Proposed steps: 1) Consolidate active open asks into canonical list (source: Sales notes, Support tickets, GitHub issues). 2) Define scoring matrix with weighted axes (customer value, engineering effort, security/regulatory complexity, polyglot coverage). 3) Draft a one-page intake form to collect required signals from customer-facing teams. 4) Run two-week pilot triage cycle with Triage working group (PM, Eng leads for SDK/runtime, one Design rep). 5) Produce prioritized backlog and publish decisions to stakeholders with rationale and next steps.

Notes on constraints and risks: - Private deployments often require stricter auth patterns (KMS, customer-managed token rotation) — score higher on engineering cost. - Streaming ergonomics requests can conflict with runtime batch/caching SLOs; require Eng sign-off on perf/regression risk. - Language requests create ongoing maintenance burden; favor languages with existing community bindings or clear strategic indicators.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical inventory (list) of active enterprise SDK requests consolidated into one sheet with source links (sales/support/PR) and initial owner assigned
Published scoring rubric (weights and descriptions) agreed by PM, two SDK engineers, and Design

Intake form (Google Form / Confluence template) that captures customer details: account, revenue tier, security needs, deployment mode (hosted/dedicated/private), expected QPS, latency needs, and minimal reproducible example
Pilot run completed with at least 8 enterprise requests triaged and each assigned a rank and recommended next step (implement, schedule, defer, or decline), with justification
Prioritized backlog exported to Linear with clear champions and estimated effort buckets (small/medium/large), and stakeholder announcement published with link to decisions
Handoff checklist created for each ‘accept to implement’ item containing acceptance tests, perf/regression guardrails, and required design touchpoints
